title: e2e-latency-profiling-traces-2026-03-12-iter2
body:
Purpose:
Run #2 of our end-to-end latency trace collection and initial analysis for the serving runtime. Goal: validate tail sources (p95/p99) across realistic production traffic shape and get a per-stage breakdown to drive short-term mitigations.

Summary of dataset:
- Collection window: 2026-03-11 23:00 -> 2026-03-12 06:00 (UTC) across prod-region-us-west and prod-region-eu-west.
- Total requests captured: 112,482 (sampled to 50k for trace export).
- Workloads: chat-style multi-turn (avg tokens generated 64), single-turn generation (avg 16), and embedding requests (lightweight, excluded from most traces).
- Instrumentation: client-side timestamp, ingress proxy, router, per-model-pool queue timestamps, model runtime enter/exit, kv-cache hit/miss markers, tokenization/serialize timings.

Aggregation methodology:
- Latencies are wall-clock ms from client-send to client-receive.
- Per-stage latencies are computed from adjacent instrumentation events; gaps are attributed to network/ingress when cross-host boundaries observed.
- Outliers: requests with >5s end-to-end were inspected separately (not removed) and kept as part of p99 calculations.
- p50/p95/p99 reported across the whole sample and by request type and by sequence-length bucket (short <32, mid 32-128, long >128).

Top-line numbers (overall, all request types combined):
- p50 = 182 ms
- p95 = 624 ms
- p99 = 1,842 ms
- Mean = 271 ms (skewed by long-tail)

Per-stage median and tail contribution (aggregate; values in ms):
- client-network (client -> ingress): p50=18, p95=70, p99=210
- ingress (proxy + auth + routing): p50=12, p95=45, p99=150
- router + routing decision: p50=6, p95=20, p99=80
- model-queue (time spent waiting in pool queue): p50=22, p95=180, p99=1,100
- model-infer (actual runtime on GPU/CPU): p50=90, p95=220, p99=380
- kv-cache lookup & prefix-hit processing: p50=6, p95=18, p99=60
- tokenization/denorm/serialize: p50=8, p95=20, p99=40
- response-serialize/egress: p50=20, p95=51, p99=122

Percent contribution to end-to-end p95 tail (qualitative):
- model-queue: ~45% of p95 extra tail (dominant for p99 on long contexts)
- model-infer runtime: ~25% (higher for long sequences and larger models)
- network+ingress: ~10% (sporadic region-specific spikes)
- serialization/tokenization/kv-cache: ~20% combined (kv-cache misses amplify model-infer cost)

Notable breakdowns by request class:
- Short requests (<32 tokens): p95 430ms, p99 1,020ms. Model-queue contributes heavily when bursts occur.
- Mid requests (32-128): p95 710ms, p99 1,900ms. Model-infer contributes more proportionally.
- Long requests (>128): p95 1,340ms, p99 3,120ms. p99 dominated by queue+inference + occasional memory GC (see anomalies).

Observed anomalies and root-candidate causes:
1) Large p99 spikes correlated with short-lived queue saturation on specific model-pools (gpu-a100-ml-4). Traces show many requests piling up for ~900ms before being scheduled -> suggests burst-handling behaviour in autoscaler/pool-sizing or a scheduling lock. (See sample traces IDs: trace-20260312-1a2b, trace-20260312-3f9c).
2) KV-cache misses: ~14% of requests had prefix KV-miss for hot prefixes (expected hit-rate ~85%); misses add ~120-250ms to end-to-end due to recompute/serialize overhead. Misses concentrated during rollout window when we saw higher cache churn.
3) Region-specific network jitter in eu-west during a 20-minute window (03:40-04:00 UTC) tied to a cross-AZ flapping event reported by infra team. Client-network p95 jumped from 70ms -> 220ms for that interval.
4) Intermittent model runtime GC-like pause (observed in p99 long traces) on CPU-based quantized execution path; we suspect occasional CPU-side memory reclamation during large context decoding.
5) A couple of traces show large serialization time (200-400ms) due to deep JSON structure + extremely long tool-call outputs (edge cases from a customer test).

Correlation with recent changes:
- RLINF-342 (dynamic pool rebalancer) was deployed 2026-03-10; traces show transient irregular queueing patterns that line up with rebalancer's adjustment windows. Suspect tuning needed for cooldowns and burst detection.
- PR #867 (kernel selection heuristic update) rolled to prod 2026-03-09; model-infer median improved slightly for mid requests but does not address queue tails.

Immediate mitigations suggested (short-term, low-risk):
- Increase min-pool-size for high-traffic model-pools during peak hours (owner: Aisha; ticket RLINF-355). Expected p95 reduction by ~15-25% for short/mid requests.
- Add fast-path to avoid KV-cache eviction churn during rollouts: pin hot prefixes for 2 minutes (owner: Priya; ticket RLINF-358). Expected to reduce KV-miss rate and save ~120ms per miss.
- Tighten rebalancer cooldown: increase cooldown window from 30s -> 120s while we iterate on heuristics (owner: Miguel; RLINF-357). This should smooth transient queue spikes.
- Add guard for extreme JSON outputs in serializer (truncate large tool outputs with warning flag) to avoid 200-400ms spike cases (owner: Jordan; RLINF-360).

Medium-term fixes (next sprint):
- Profiling deeper into model-pool scheduler to find lock contention hotspots; add metrics for per-pool scheduling waits. (owner: eng-serving-runtime infra subgroup)
- Investigate CPU-quantized runtime pauses: collect finer-grained heap/allocator metrics and add a jittered periodic pre-touch to avoid large reclamation events. (owner: applied-ml)
- Adaptive batching: implement a short-window adaptive batch size that detects sudden burst spikes and temporarily favors low-latency scheduling. Prototype RLINF-372.

Data quality notes / limitations:
- Sampling bias: we sampled traces to 50k due to export limits; abnormalities could be under/overrepresented in tail analysis.
- Instrumentation gaps: a small proportion (~0.7%) of requests missing one or more instrumentation events were reconstructed by best-effort attribution and flagged. Those are included but marked in the trace exports.

Next steps / action items (owners + due dates):
- Aisha: roll min-pool-size change to canary (RLINF-355) — due 2026-03-15
- Priya: implement hot-prefix pinning in KV-cache layer (RLINF-358) — due 2026-03-18
- Miguel: revert rebalancer cooldown change in canary and monitor (RLINF-357) — due 2026-03-14
- Jordan: add serializer guard and create synthetic test for large-tool-output (RLINF-360) — due 2026-03-16
- Applied-ML: enable allocator tracing on one canary pool to capture GC-like pauses (RLINF-365) — due 2026-03-19

Attachments / artifacts:
- Full sampled trace export (internal S3): s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026-03-12/e2e-sampled-50k.json.gz
- Short sample CSV with aggregated per-stage percentiles: s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026-03-12/e2e-aggregates.csv
- Heatmap visualizations and per-pool timelines: linked in Confluence page (see linked_artifacts).

Notes / open questions for the next review meeting:
- Does the team want to treat pool-sizing adjustments as an automated response (scale-up on burst) or prefer conservative manual canaries? Pros/cons and SRE risk assessment needed.
- Should we instrument a lightweight per-request priority tag to allow low-latency requests to skip large-batch formation?

Quick reproduction steps for a suspected queue saturation case:
1) From lab, replay a burst of 600 concurrent short requests against gpu-a100-ml-4 pool with the same routing policy used in prod (script: tools/loadtests/burst_short_600.sh).
2) Collect traces and observe model-queue times; confirm if queue spikes match the ~900ms patterns.
3) Toggle rebalancer cooldown in testbed and re-run to validate smoothing.

Summary (one line): p95/p99 tail is dominated by transient model-pool queue saturation and kv-cache miss amplification; short-term mitigations (pool sizing + cache pinning + rebalancer cooldown) are likely to materially reduce tail while we iterate on scheduler/batching improvements.

End of notes.
